findings.problem: A timeout on the caller-facing CompletionStage promise need not complete the source stage that the breaker records.
findings.consequence: Caller timeouts can coexist with zero recorded failures and later source success accounting.
findings.change: Trace the actual completion boundary, explain source versus returned promise, preserve shared-stage ownership, and distinguish future completion from transport termination.

findings.problem: Consecutive thresholds were described as reacting faster without configuration qualifications.
findings.consequence: May select a policy using an unsupported universal speed comparison.
findings.change: Compare actual thresholds against representative outcome sequences, false-open frequency and detection time.

findings.problem: Existing timeout advice did not provide the targeted source/wrapper contrast.
findings.consequence: A test checking only the final TimeoutException can pass while the breaker observes no timeout.
findings.change: Add caller/source/metrics assertions for both placements, late completion and bounded cleanup.

cases.commonActorTask: Operators report that inventory callers time out while breaker failure counts stay at zero. Review the actual async wiring in InventoryClient.java and the pinned dependency. Correct it only if the report is reproduced; add a focused regression check with a controllable source future. Preserve thresholds, caller-visible TimeoutException and dependency versions. Do not contact a live dependency.
cases.commonFixture: Java 21 project with Resilience4j circuitbreaker/core 2.2.0 and SLF4J 2.0.9 (available cache); one persistent CircuitBreaker configured with count window 1, minimum 1, failure threshold 50, slow duration one minute, recordException(e -> e instanceof TimeoutException). InventoryClient.fetch() obtains a fresh pending CompletableFuture<String> from an injected stub supplier. Stub can expose and complete that future later. No retries/fallback. Existing test checks only that the caller receives an ExecutionException caused by TimeoutException within 2 seconds; it does not check breaker/source state.

evaluatorOnly.expected: Trace source versus returned promise and reproduce unchanged breaker counts after outer timeout while source remains pending; late source success is still recorded. Fix places the dependency timeout where the breaker observes it (or an equivalently justified design) without threshold changes. New regression independently checks caller exception, source state, counted failure and open state.
